content.value_statement: Genomic interval machine learning requires careful preprocessing, model selection, and validation. This skill guides Geniml workflows for BED embeddings, scATAC-seq analysis, and consensus peaks.
actual_capabilities: Guides Region2Vec tokenization, training, and embedding evaluation for BED file collections.
Explains BEDspace preprocessing, training, distance calculation, and search workflows.
Supports scEmbed planning for single-cell ATAC-seq embeddings and scanpy integration.
Compares consensus peak universe methods, including CC, CCF, ML, and HMM approaches.
Documents BBClient caching, BEDshift randomization, tokenization utilities, and evaluation metrics.
limitations: Requires Geniml and related scientific Python tools to be installed in the user environment.
Does not provide datasets, genome references, or trained models directly.
Large scATAC-seq and universe-building workflows may require substantial memory and compute.
BEDspace requires a separate StarSpace installation for model training.

use_cases.title: Build BED Region Embeddings
use_cases.description: Prepare BED files, tokenize regions against a universe, train Region2Vec, and review embedding quality metrics.

use_cases.title: Cluster scATAC-seq Cells
use_cases.description: Plan scEmbed preprocessing, train cell embeddings, and connect the output to scanpy clustering and visualization.

use_cases.title: Create Consensus Peak Universes
use_cases.description: Choose a universe-building method and tune cutoff, merge, and filter parameters for consistent downstream tokenization.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner user selecting a Geniml method.
prompt_templates.prompt: I have BED files and metadata for genomic regions. Help me choose between Region2Vec, BEDspace, scEmbed, and universe building.

prompt_templates.title: Train Region2Vec
prompt_templates.scenario: User has BED files and a universe file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Region2Vec workflow for my BED files. Include tokenization, training parameters, output files, and validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan scEmbed Analysis
prompt_templates.scenario: User is preparing single-cell ATAC-seq data.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me prepare an scEmbed analysis for an AnnData scATAC-seq dataset with peak coordinates, tokenization, training, and scanpy integration.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Universe Methods
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare CC, CCF, ML, and HMM universe-building methods for my ATAC-seq peak collection, then recommend parameters and quality checks.

output_examples.input: Plan a Region2Vec workflow for 40 ATAC-seq BED files and a project universe.
output: Recommended hard tokenization against the project universe before training.
Suggested starting values for embedding dimension, context length, shuffling count, and learning rate.
Listed validation checks for token coverage, silhouette score, and downstream clustering review.

output_examples.input: Help me decide how to build a consensus peak universe from mixed ATAC-seq samples.
output: Recommended starting with coverage cutoff for fast inspection.
Explained when to move to CCF or ML for noisy boundaries or publication-quality analysis.
Provided checks for merge distance, minimum peak size, and genome assembly consistency.

output_examples.input: Prepare an scEmbed workflow for an AnnData scATAC-seq dataset.
output: Outlined required peak coordinate fields and tokenization output.
Suggested training settings based on dataset scale.
Explained how to store embeddings for scanpy neighbors, clustering, and UMAP.

best_practices: Validate BED coordinates, genome assembly, and universe coverage before training models.
Record parameters, random seeds, input file versions, and model outputs for reproducibility.
Use multiple evaluation metrics and biological labels before trusting embedding clusters.
anti_patterns: Training embeddings before checking tokenization coverage and genome assembly consistency.
Using BEDspace without verifying metadata file names match the BED input files.
Treating UMAP plots as proof of biological validity without quantitative and domain validation.

faq.question: What data does this skill focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on genomic interval data, mainly BED files, scATAC-seq peak matrices, metadata tables, and consensus peak universes.

faq.question: Does the skill run Geniml automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance and command examples. The user or agent must run tools in a prepared environment.

faq.question: When should I use Region2Vec?
faq.answer: Use Region2Vec when you need unsupervised embeddings for genomic regions or BED file collections without metadata-aware search.

faq.question: When should I use BEDspace?
faq.answer: Use BEDspace when BED files have metadata labels and you need joint region-label search or similarity analysis.

faq.question: What does scEmbed add?
faq.answer: scEmbed creates cell-level embeddings from single-cell ATAC-seq data and can store results for scanpy workflows.

faq.question: What are the main setup requirements?
faq.answer: You need Geniml, scientific Python dependencies, valid BED or AnnData inputs, genome references, and StarSpace for BEDspace training.
